### 59.Gal. 5'6a trans

Jonathan Edwards

Galat. 5. 6. for in Jesus X Neither Circumcision Availeth Any thing nor Uncircimcision but faith that Worketh by Love

______________

It seems that there were some false teachers Risen up that had been amongst the Galatians endeavouring to Instill into them that it was necessary in order to their Justification and salvation that they should be Circumcised and observe Conform to the Legal observances and Rites of the Law of moses and Particularly that they should be Circumcised.

______________________

This doctrine tending to make the Grace of God in God Lose and Overthrowing the sufficiency of Jesus X for salvation and being directly Contrary to that Great doctrine of the Gospel Justification by faith. the Apostle Writes this Epistle to them to bring them off from those Principles and Insists very much upon Upon the Contrary doctrine of Justification only by faith. and upon the Useflessness and vanity of wo the works of the Law to that End, and the danger of depending on Legal Performances. And And in this Chapter he is upon the same Arguments stand fast says he in the first verse in the liberty where with X hath made you free and be not Entangled Again with [^001-note1] the Yoke of bondage. that is the stand Resolutely in Resolutely maintain Resolutely the liverty which X has Given us from the Burdensome Legal services. and to your liberty from the Covenant of works that you may not be Obliged by that either perfectly to Obey the Law or else to suffer the Penalty of it. Behold I Paul says he in the 2d verse testify unto you say unto you If ye be Circumcised X shall Profit you nothing. If you think Circumcision is necessary to your justi in order to Your Justification and that to the Gospel of Jesus X is not sufficient without it and have a dependance upon that to Justify You partly to Justify you X will profit you nothing youll Recieve no benefit by him whom you think not sufficient alone for Your salvation

He Goes on in the 3d verse for I testify unto Every man that is Circumcised that he is a debtor to the Whole Law. that is by seeking to be Justified by that or Any other work he Puts himself under the Covenant of works and is a debtor either perfectly to Obey the Law which is Im to bring forth Perfect Obedience or to suffer the Penalty of the Law for X is ( as he Goes on in the 4th verse is become of [^001-note2] no Effect to you whosoever of you Are Justified by the Law ye are fallen from Grace. for seeing ye have dependance upon the works you have nothing to do with free Grace nor will you have Any benefit by that which you [Gal. 5:6 (1)] [^001-note3] have no dependance Upon

II Tis Only an efficacious working faith that Avails any thing before God. by an Efficacious working faith we mean that that prod Does the proper work of faith in the heart and brings for forth the proper fruits of it [^001-note14] in the life. There is a faith that is Lifeless. barren & Ineffectual makes no Great or Lasting alteration in the heart or life

The proper work of faith in the heart is to Change and Renew the heart. to work a new nature to take off the heart and affections from Earthly things and to make them heavenly. to make the heart humble. holy, humble, patient, submissive, meek, Charitable, such a disposition as this is the natureal wo Genuine work of true Xtian faith and this is what of' An effectual faith will produce Galatian 5 22 23 But the fruit of the spirit is Love Joy, peace, Longsuffering, Gentleness, Goodness, faith. meekness, temperance.

Next Place we proceeded to Prove that the world will thus Come to An End and we took notice of two Arguments from Reason that Renderd it at Least very Probable that the world would not Last alwaies. 1 we showed that the world in its Own Nature is not a thing Everlastingly durable. and that it was of such a nature that without a miracle to pre preserve or Renew it it Could not Last alwaies [^003-note31] 2 That this world is a Corrupted degenerated and Corrupted world. and that it was very much in a Ruind Confused state and that therefore it is not Probable that God would suffer it to Last Alwaies But then 2dly we Observed that the scrip ture Put it Past all manner of doubt. in that as much as by that we Are taught that this world is But of a temporary Use. being only for a state of trial for another world and a state of Prepar Place of Preparation of the Elect for heaven. and that the scripture did Plai often Plainly Declare this very thing that the world should Come to An End and also Gives us an ac ccount of all the most notable Events that fall out in the world till that very time and not only so but Gives us a particular description of the manner how it should be ____________________________ whic was the viz the manner of its Coming to Third thing that we Insisted upon. and Observed that in the 1st Place there would be the Great and General Judgment Xs descending from heaven Clothed with divine majesty and Glory with all the holy Angels with him and that the dead should be Raised at the sound of the Last trumpet & should be brought before the Judgment seat both small and Great. And should be Judged according to their works and sentenced some to Everlasting life and others to Everlasting Burnings 2 that the world being About to Come to a dissolution the Earth should be terribly shaken 3 That the World should be dissolved by fire That the Earth and all the Works that Are therin should be burnt up an That the Earth and Air should all Involved in flames And the Air filld [^003-note32] with them & 4 That the visible heavens should Also Pass away. & The Fourth and Last thing we spoke to was the state of those that were Once the Inhabitants of the world after it dissolution. and 1 . we Observed that Gods Treaty the Present dispensation of Grace and Gods Treaty with mankind about their salvation should then Come to an Everlasting End & 2. That the Good and the Bad should be everlastingly separated one from Another & 3. That they should be in Exceeding different Conditions. ## 64. Hab. 1:13(a)

### 64.Hab. 1'13a trans

Jonathan Edwards

Hab. 1 . 13. Thou Artnt of Purer Eyes than to behold Evil And Canst not Look On Iniquity

________________

The Prophet speaking of the Great Prevailing of the Land of Israel in the beginning of the Chapter fortells the dreadfull destruction that God Would bring Upon them for their wickedness By the Chaldeans . I Behold I will work a work in Your days. says God by the Prophet which Ye will not believe tho it be told You for Lo I will Raise Up the Chaldeans that Bitter and hasty Nation which shall march through the Breadth of the Land to Possess the dwel ling Places that Are not theirs.----- And he Goes on to tell how dreadfull their Army shall be that shall Come Against Judea and how Great the destruction which they will make. But as he takes Notice in the 11 The Chaldeans shall Impute this Power of to Hisr Own God. and shall Attribute it to Hisr Idols that they Are thus overco are thus Able to Overcome and destroy the Land. Then shall his mind Change and he shall Pass over and offend. Imputing this Power Unto his. The King of Babilon will boast exceedingly that his God is stronger than Israels God. so that God that had been so famed for the Great things that he had done for that [^005-note1] People but Yet that nevertheless for all his defence he was Able to overcome that People that he defended This makes the Prophet speak as he does in the following Verses. Art Not thou from Everlasting O Lord my God mine holy One. we shall not die. O Lord thou hast ordained them for Judgment. and O mighty God thou hast Established them for Correction. Tho they think thei tis their Gods that Give them Victory. and that it is because their Idols are stronger than these that they Are Able to overcome thy People. yet thou Art the Everlasting God And it is not because their Gods help them to Overcome thy Pep People but because thou makest use of them for their Correction of thy People. And In the text he Pleads and verses following he pleads with God that he would Punish and disap the Proud Boastings of his peoples Enemies And the Unjust viz treachery and Cruelty of hi these his Peoples Enemies and that he would not suffer them to have success in their Let them alone to triumphe over his heritage

_________________________________

and here we may Observe What is the Argument he the prophet makes use with God to plead that that he would frown upon them in their wickedness and that is the holiness of God and his hatred of sin seeing God was of so holy a nature that he Cant Give any Countenance to sin he prays that he Would not [^005-note2] Countenance the Chaldeans in their Us Proudly and Cruelly. murdering and destroying the Nations of the world. Here Gods hatred of sin is expressed by a beautifull map metaphor of his not being Able Look on it he hates it so exceedingly those things that men Love they love to Look Upon and What they exceedingly hate and Loath they Cant bear to look Upon they'll turn away their Eyes from it they Cant bear to see it so God does as it were so Loath sin and Abominate sin that he Cant bear to see it. By Gods not being Able to behold or Look on sin is meant that it is impossible that God should Give Any Countenance to it. or that he should any way manifest any favour or approbation of it. this Appears by the words Immediately following wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously that is wherefore dost thou seem as if thou Approved It of then what they do by suffering of them to prosper in their wickedness designs

The Reason that is here Given Why God Cant look upon sin is because he is of Purer Eyes than to do that is Gods nature is so pure and holy that it n a is impossible but that he should Loath and abhor sin Doc That God hates Sin [^005-note3]

Under this doctrine we shall 1 show what is meant by Gods Hating sin & 2 we shall Give the Reasons Why he hates it

I We shall show what is Intended when it is said God hates sin. and there Are these following things Implied in it Gods nature is exceeding Contrary to it 1 That tis exceeding Contrary to God nature. Contrariety of nature is the foundation of all hatred. all beings hate those things that Are Contrary to their nature. and to which their natures Are Contrary. and love those things that Are Agreable to their nature they naturally and necessarily do it. if we so Angels Wicked men hate those things that Are Contrary to their nature as th and Good men hate those things that they their natures are Contrary to their natures Angels hate those things that Are Contrary to their natures and devils those things that are Contrary to their Natures or that their Natures are Contrary to. hatred that is the very notion of hatred. Contrariety and opposition of mind to a thing. it would be a Contradiction there fore to suppose that Any one should not hate that that his nature is Contrary to. so Gods hatred is the Contrariety of his nature unto sin being Contrary to sin. God dont hate a thing for being distant from all beings are infinitely distant from God in that they Are Infinitely below him but for being Contrary to him. that [^005-note4] may be Infinite distance where there is no Opposition

__________________

Now sin is exceeding Contrary to the nature of God. u there is no Opposition or Contrariety that Can be thought of more direct than this. tis Contrary as light is to darkness for God is light and sin is darkness yea tis more Contrary abundantly than Any external light light and darkness that we percieve with our bodily eyes. more Contrary than the brightness of the sun of in a Clear day so the Grossest darkness blackest darkness because Gods bright ness and his Glory is far Greater more bright Infinitely t more than the light of the sun and therefore is Infinitely Contrary The Reason of it is because God is holiness it self and there fore his nature must be most directly Contrary to wickedness and he is not only holiness it self but he is infinite holiness. he is an Infinite Purity. excellency and beauty. the moon and stars look very bright and Clear and pure but if we say saw the purity and brightness of Gods holiness the moon and stars would loose their brightness Job 25 5 behold Even to the moon and it shineth not yea the stars Are not Pure in his sight The holi highest heavens Are doubtless a very pure There is no defilement Comes there but Yet we Read [^005-note5] that the heavens Are not Clean in his sight Job 15.

The very notion of sin is Contrariety to the nature of God that is a Good definition of sin. tis opposition to the beauty and excellency of God. sin being Contrariety to God Gods Nature must be Contrary to that and this is the first thing that is meant by Gods hatred of sin

2 When it is said God hate sin Another thing Implied is that Gods Nature its in such is the nature of its Impossible that God should Any Way favour or Countenance he Cant Encourage it or smile upon it those things that men hate they dont use to Countenance or Encourage. that which a king hates he wont Encourage in his Chilsubjects and that which a fathers hates he wont favour and smile upon in his Children. so God never Gives any Countenance or Encouragement to sin, and he not Only dont do it but it is impossible he should his nature is such that he Cant smile upon sin he Cant favour sin in words by speaking favourably of it. or speaking of it so as to mitigate it or to excuse it he Cant favour it in his providence or do Any thing so that any Can Reasonably take Encouragement from it to Go on in sin. in this sense God is of Purer Eyes than to behold evil and Can not look on Iniquity [^005-note6]

3 When it is said that God hates sin. it is implied that tis the Will of God to Remove sin at a distance from him we dont love the Presence of things that persons hate they dont love the Presence of them, they dont love to have em near to 'em . what a person exceedingly loaths they Endeavour to shun and Avoid & to have at a distance from him. and to they Cant bear to have it in their sight nor to have so near as to be in the way of Any Communication. so God hates sin and therefore tis his will and tis his method to Remove sin far a way from him. by Casting those that have the Guilt of sin of sin or those that Retain the filth of it out away out of his sight by dra driving of he never suffers those that are not Cleansed from sinners and that Are not Cleansed from this filthiness to Remain in his Presence. but alwaies drives them far from him. Psal 5. 4 for thou Art a God that hast no pleasure in wickedness Neither shall evil dwell with thee. so the Angels that sinned they were Immediately Cast out of Gods sight Cast from heaven down to the because hell so Adam when he sinned was Ca driven out of the Garden that was a place of Gods Peculiar presence so the Children of Israel when they Grew Corrupt they [^005-note7] were Removed Out of God sight. 2 kings 17 18 so wicked shall at death and Judgment be as it were Cast away out of Gods sight. he will say depart ye Cu from me ye workers of Inquity. and depart ye Cursed. They Cant be Removed Away from Gods essential Presence for so God is Every where. God is so in hell as wel as to his being and Essence in hell as well as any Where else. but when we say they Are Removed at a distance from God we mean that they Are Removed far away from all Communion from all manifestation of Gods Gracious Presence . and Gracious Communication or manifestation. Tis Gods Irresistable will and Perpetual method to thus to Remove sin far from him. and sinners that are not Cleansed

4 & Lastly when it is said that God hates sin it is implied that tis Gods Immutable Purpose to be PruPunish sin. the Commission of sin stirs up the Anger and wrath of God it kindls his fury and he is unchangeably Resolved to Give a testimony of his hatred of all sin and his Indignation Against it. Exodus 3 he Evermore Punishes sin he Lets No sin Escape without punishment. then never any sin Appears in the world but [^005-note8] God will be Avenged of it Exodus 7 That will in no wise Clear the Guilty. God Punishes the sin of the fallen Angels and th he Punishes the sin of men of Good men as well as bad men Good mens sins Are Punished by the sufferings of X and Bad mens by their own Eternal sufferings. y God is Resolved unchangeably Resolved to punish sin with an Infinite Punishment Every sin with Eternal destruction or that thats Equivalent to it. so that his hatred is as it were Infinite in as much as the tokens of it are infinite Evil to him that has the Guilt of it upon him. and it is unalterable so that no prayers nor Cries nor tears nor Lamentations shall ever alter Gods purpose of punishing sin or mitigate Incline him to mitg mitigate the Punishment

we now Proceed in the II Place to Give the Reasons Why God hates sin & 1 God hates sin because sin Carries in it hatred of God This is the very Nature of sin Enmity or hatred to God Rom 8 7 the Carnal mind is Enmity Against God. as we said before that sin is nothing else th but the Oppo siteness and Contrariety of the disposition & God to God tis a principle of hatred to him There is nothing in God but What sin makes man Opposite [^005-note9] to they Are opposite to the holiness to of God Yea si these Are the most direct and the Greatest Contraries in the world more Contrary as we showed already than the brightness of the sun and the Greatest darkness. it makes men opposite to the wisdom and Infinite knowledge of God wicked men would be Glad if God was not Omniscient for then they would have hopes of Concealing their wickedness and of decieving of him. they Are Opposite to the power of God because if he were not so Powerfull they would have hopes of Getting out of his hands. they Are opposite to the wer mercy of God as appears very evidently by their being so exceeding difficultly brought to own be willing to be saved by meer mercy if they did not hate the meer h sovereign mercy they would Certainly accept of it. & not be striving so much to be saved by their own Righ teousness. ## 66. Jas. 1:17

### 66.Jas. 1'17 trans

Jonathan Edwards

James 1 17 --------- Cometh down from the Father of Lights ------------ Every Good Gift and every Perfect Gift Cometh down from the Father of lights with Whom is no variableness neither shadow of Change

_____

Particularly that Clause expression the Father of Lights

_______

The apostle Writing to the believing Jews that were scattered abroad amongst the Gentiles in the 5 verse he exhorts them that if Any man Lack wisdom he should ask it of God, Who Gives liberally and Upbraideth not and in the 12 verse he tells them of the blessedness of those that Endure tempta tion who shall Recieve a Crown of life of of Gai Which the Lord hath Promised to them an and in the 6 and seventh verse he tells in what manner we must Pray for ask what we want of God . It seems to be with an eye to theie exhortation of to prayer that he here puts them in mind that Every Good and perfect Gift Comes from God. by a Good Gift and a perfect is meant every thing that Gift that is for for our Real Good and Advantage there Are many things that men Are Glad of that bent for their benefit. they are Glad of means and op opportunities to satisfy their lusts but those are [^007-note1] not Good and Perfect Gifts. But Every thing that is for Our Real benefit is from Above. our bread tha not only spiritual blessings but our bread that we eat is as a from Above as well aswell as the manna that the Children of Israel Eat in the wilderness. it Come our Common And daily mercies Come down from God as Really as if it were Immediately Rained down in a miraculous manner out of heaven It Comes down from the Father of lights that is it Comes down from God it is spoken as Comparing of God to the sun, every Good Gift Comes as much from God as light Comes from the sun. as the sun in the firmament sheds Abroad his light and Enlightens the world and fills it with his benign Influence so God diffuses abroad his blessings and Influences Gracious Influences and is in a more Glorious sense the fountain of light than the sun is But the Apostle takes notice of one thing Particularly wherin this spiritual fountain of light differs from the sun the Corporeal fountain of light and that is that in him is no variableness nor shadow of turning. the sun is a variable fountain of light some as to us sometimes is shiny and sometimes [^007-note2] it Doth not shine. the sun Rises and sets but and is subject to Variable Revolutions. but God is as a sun always fixd that tur in the hemisphere that shines without Interruption when it is & when it is said he is without shadow of turning the meaning is without shadow by turning. the sun by turning Round in the heavens Leaves us in the shadows of the night. But God is a sun that without such turnings as are attended with shadows he is light without shado shadows nothing but light 1 John 15 1, 5. God is light and in him is no darkness at all

____

it is said that he is the Father of lights. it is a he brew way of expressions it was Common in the hebrew Language when they would set forth the excellency of a thing to speak of it in the Plural Number so when it said the Father of Lights and not the father of Light the meaning is the Author of Glo Glorious light. or is may signifie that God is the Fountain of all sorts of Lights. there Are various kinds of Light God is the fountain of them all as we shall show under this doctrine ----------- Doc That God is the Father of Lights [^007-note3]

____

Herea we shall First explain more Generally what is meant by his being the Father of lights &

________________________________

Secondly show Particularly what Lights he is that father or Author of

_______

But I we shall explain more Generally & 1 When it is said that God is the Father of Lights it signifies that he is Essentially a very Glorious being. Light or brightness signifies Glory the Glory of the sun and of the moon and stars is their light or brightness the sun is the most Glorious being that we behold in the material world because ha of his Great brightness. and there fore the sun used Commonly amongst the heathen to be worshipped as God. but God is exceedingly more Glorious. the light which Paul beheld was above the brightness of the sun. the brightness of Gods Glory is so Great and so excellent that we Cant Concieve of it. God Arrayeth himself with light as with light as with a Garment, Ps 104 2 when God Used to Appear Under the Old Testament he Used to appear as all arrayed in light to signify his Glory we Read that in the wilderness from time to time the Glory of the Lord Appeared that is there was a Great brightness brightness Appeard that signified Gods Glory [^007-note4] God is as it were Arrayed with an Infinite brightness a brightness that dont Create Pain as the light of the sun Pains the Eyes to behold it but Rather fills with excess of Joy and Delight. Indeed no man Can see God and live because the sight of such Glory would Overpower Nature but tis because the Joy and Pleasure in bel beholding it would be too strong for natu a frail nature --------------------------- God God has this Glory ess 2 God is a Communicative essentially and of himself. he is Independently and necessariy Glory Glorious the sun is Glorious but he derives that Glory from Another but God is Glorious in and of himself and so is the Fa ther of Glory

_____________________________________________________________

2 God is a Communicative being. Light is Communicative or Rather a Communication from the Luminary the sun Communicates himself to the world by light. he sheds abroad and diffused around his light or brightness and fills the world with his beneficial Influences Enlightens and Enlivens and Comforts the Universe God is like the sun in this Respect he is Abundantly Communicative he is a fountain of Goodness Continual ly scattering abroad his Goodness. and diffusing of his bounty plentifully and Continually and Abundantly as the sun diffuses his Rays. as the light of the [^007-note5] sun fills the world so does Gods Goodness Gods Goodness is most extensive and Universal Reaches to all sorts of Creatures he opens his bountifull hand and satisfies the desires of Every living thing. he feeds men and me beast and bear and provides for angels and men and the beasts of the Earth and fowls of the Air and fishes of the sea and for Insects. as the sun shines Continually so Gods Goodness is Continual his mercy Endureth forever Yea God Communicates himself more Continually than the sun for as the sun turns from us in Leaves a shadow it ha but God is without a shadow of turning God has in himself an Infinite fullness and sufficiency and he is an Infinite and his fullness is Continually overflowing he is an Infinite fountain and a fountain Perpetually sending Out Pure streams Gods Communicativeness is of two things of excellency of & of happiness God is an Incomprehensible fountain of both. he Communicates excellency to the Creature he beautifies and adorns the world as the sun adorns' the world with his Rays all the perfection and all the excellency that is to be discoverd among men or angels or any other Creature is a Communication of this fountain as Rays are Communicated[^007-note6] from the sun. all Creatures Recieve their excellency from God as the moon and Planets have their light from the sun so God Communicates happiness. being Infinitely happy in himself he Rejoices and blesses all others the Rays that stream forth from this sun are as it were streams of h Pleasure and happiness. God is a fountain of happiness and he is the only fountain of happiness

_______________________________________________________

II We propose to show Particularly. What lights God. is the father of & 1 He is the Father of Jesus X the brightness of his Glory and the light of the world. ## 69. Matt. 10:28

### 69.Matt. 10'28 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Math 10 28 ---------- Fear him Which is Able to destroy both body an soul in hell

____________________

X is sending forth the Apostles to Te Teach and do miracles . and to declare to the world the kingdom of God . and he forwarns them what troubles and Persecutions they Are like to meet with and that they shall not only be persecuted in Lesser degrees but shall be Put to death for him . what he says in this verse is to strengthen and Encourage them 'em and strength en 'em against these Persecutions . One the one hand he tells two how little he uses two Arguments to strengthen them on the One hand he tells them how little the wrath of men is to be Regarded in that the utmost that they Can do is to kill the body but bent able to kill the soul this is that they might not be terrified from the Profession of the Gospel by their Persecutions . On the other hand he tells 'em how dread full Gods wrath is who is able to do more than to kill is able also to destroy not only both soul and body in hell he tells em this that they might be afraid to deny the Gospel upon any Account whatever because if they do they will expose themselves to this dreadfull[^010-note1] wrath and to these affects of it. The words are to be understood not only that God is meerly able to do it but that he will do it to all to all that Cast off the deny Jesus X and Cast off the Gospel. It Implies thus much in the manner that it is spoken, for as X knows by the former expression that they should not fear them that are able to kill the body he mean'd their Persecutors that were Disposed to do it so by this Latter expression. he means that that they should fear him that Can sell both b destroy both body and soul in hell he means him who Can and will to all those that deny them faith It Implies that tis Gods method so to do tis according to his Law a punishment that is appointed and ordain'd for such otherwise they there is no force in the Argu ment . Therefore the doctrine we shall speaks to at this time is this

## 71. Rom. 2:16 (edit)

### The Secrets of Men Must All Come Into Judgment Before God Romans 2:16. In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel. The Apostle is speaking in the foregoing verses, beginning with the sixth verse, how God will judge all sorts of men universally according to their deeds; that he will render indignation and wrath, tribulation and anguish upon everyone that doth evil, whether he be Jew or Gentile; and on the contrary will render glory, honor and peace to every soul that works good, whether he be Jew or Gentile, for there is no respect of persons with God [Rom. 2:9-11]. God won’t favor the Jews because they are the seed of Abraham, nor shall the Gentiles be excused because of their ignorance. For says the Apostle, “as many as have sinned without law shall perish without law” [Rom. 2:12].  That is, they shall perish for their breach of the law of nature, written in their hearts; as the Apostle afterwards explains himself, “and as many as have sinned under[i] the law shall be judged by the law,” as in the twelfth verse. What follows in three next verses comes in by way of parenthesis, and the words of our text are to be connected with the twelfth verse. There, he told by what rule they should be judged; in our text he tells the time when: “in the day when God shall judge the secrets of men according to my gospel.”

 

 

 

 

 

This day is deciphered,
1. By the business of the day, which is judgment. It will be day appointed for this very end and business; it is a day to be noted for the great work of it. And therefore it is called the great and notable day, Acts 2:20.
2. The judge, who is Jesus Christ, that crucified man[ii] that the Apostle preached to the Romans.
3. The things judged, namely, the secrets of men; things that are out of the way of other judgments that human judges can have nothing to do with, because they are secret and hid from the world.
4. The revelation which God has made of it, which the Apostle calls his gospel, that is, the gospel which he had preached. As if he had said, “It will be on that day that I have told you of and preached to you, and which has been so clearly revealed in that gospel that I have preach[ed] to you and to other Gentiles.”

DOCTRINE.
The secrets of men must all come into judgment before God.
Under this doctrine we shall,
I. Show what is implied in a thing’s coming into judgment before God.
II. [Show] what secrets of men will thus come into judgment before God.And then make improvement.
I. There are these things implied in the secrets of men coming in to judgment before God:
First. That God will bring ‘em to light and call men to an account concerning ‘em. They must appear before God and be inquired of about ‘em, as it was with our first parents. They hid themselves, and endeavor to keep themselves and what they had done secret; but God calls ‘em out of their lurking place and inquires, “Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat?” [Gen. 3:11], and, “What is this that thou hast done? [Gen. 3:13].
There are innumerable things concerning every man that are hid from the eye of the world they know nothing about, therefore they are called to an account by nobody concerning 'em. They are not cognizable by parents, or by the civil magistrates, or by the church. He escapes punishment and reproof, and the man is no otherwise looked upon than if they had not been: but they are open and naked to the eyes of God. And he therefore, in due time, will call to an account about 'em. They must come and stand before God’s seat, must stand at his bar. God won’t want witnesses to make them evident, for they were seen by his own all-seeing eye.
Now God says nothing to ‘em about it, though he sometimes executes judgments upon men for their secret wickedness in this world, and speaks to men by his word and by providence and by their own consciences; yea,[iii] speaks once, yea, twice, but they perceive it not. But there will a time come, when God will apparently and immediately plead with them about their secret things.
Things that were secret must be brought to light before God, they must be made public; they were known to God before, but they shall be made known to angels and men in God’s presence, and the persons themselves being present. Luke 12:2-3, “There is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; nor hid, that shall not be known. Whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.” Men won’t be called to an account before God for his information, but for the manifestation of their guilt—an inexcusableness. He won’t ask sinners the reasons of their actions that he may be informed, but that it may appear that they have no reasons nor any excuse, or if they have obtained satisfaction and pardon. They must be called to an account, that their freedom from guilt may appear by the good account which they have to give. Rom. 14:12, “So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.” Matt. 12:36, “Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” It is called a reckoning with men. Matt. 25:19, ”After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.” So God will reckon with men, with every man, about all their secret disposition and actions, that are included in[iv] judging of ‘em.
Second. A determining the nature of them. Whether they are agreeable or disagreeable to the divine law, whether they are agreeable or contrary to the light of nature and the light of divine revelation, whether the actions are good or sinful, to that end the books of God’s law will be opened, Rev. 20:12.
It will be determined to what degree they are bad; the aggravating circumstances will be reckoned[v] up and every one will have its due weight given to it. Everything, whether it before was secret or open, shall be made to appear just as it is, shall be set forth in its true light and proper labors.[vi]
Therefore judging is called weighing in the balances. Dan. 5:27, “Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.”
Third. There is a determining the recompense that is due by the divine law, and sentencing of him accordingly. It shall be determined, according to those books which shall be opened, what reward or punishment belongs to him upon the account. The same rule, that is the rule for us to live by, will be the rule for us to be judged by hereafter.
And the powerful sentence shall immediately be passed; they shall be doomed to receive the appointed recompense. And the eternal reward or punishment shall be irreversibly fixed.
Fourth. There is included in divine judging, executing the sentence; for the same person who passes sentence by his almighty power, executes the same. The sentence does as it were procure the execution. As God by his word created the world—he said, “Let it be,” and it was so—by his word or sentence he will as it were procure the execution of it. God’s executing his decree of judgment is frequently called “judging” in scripture, as you may see, Job 36:31, and in many other places. We shall in the
II. [Second] place show what secrets of men those are, that shall come into judgment before God. He will thoroughly try men’s state. The eye of this judge will search me[vii] and discern [Matt. 7:1-2].
First. God will hereafter judge the state and condition that men are in in this world. The state of men’s souls is a secret thing in this world. We see the outward behavior of men, some of it, but we see not the heart; the principles and spiritual disposition, and state of the soul is out of sight.
Concerning[viii] some men, indeed, we may have reason from our constant observation of their vicious lives, of their allowed, high-handed, presumptuous, wicked course of life, to be confident and to conclude that they are wicked men. Though we can’t be assured what state they die in, however they have lived.
From the contrary, holy, Christian walk and behavior of others, we may have great reason to hope that they are truly godly, and sometimes we may be very fully satisfied; but we can’t be certain concerning others. Though there be a possibility of persons’ obtaining assurance concerning themselves, yet they can’t be sure concerning others. And in the general, the spiritual condition of men’s souls in is[ix] one of the secrets of men. It is a hidden, invisible thing; the life of [a] Christian is a hidden life. Col. 3:3, “Your life is hid with Christ in God.” A saint is said to receive “a new name, which no man knows but he that receives it,” Rev. 2:17. The heart is called “the hidden man,” I Pet. 3:4. The most skillful persons, and they that have had most experience, can’t certainly tell, and very of ten persons are ignorant concerning themselves. They don’t know the condition of their own souls; they frequently are pure in their own eyes, when indeed, they are not cleansed from their filthiness; they think they are rich and increased with goods, and know not that they are wretched and miserable, and poor and blind and naked [Rev. 3:17]. There are multitudes that are mistaken about their condition; they know not their own hearts. And there are many that are truly godly that don’t know it; they hope they are, but they have also many doubts and fears, and sometimes conclude themselves wrong when they are indeed right. So that the state and condition of men’s souls is in the general a secret thing in this world.
But there is a time coming when it will appear what every man is. His heart, which lay hid and out of sight, shall be laid open and plain to view, so that all may see what his spiritual condition is. Then it will be tried, whether the man had any sincerity in him or no. And then it shall appear, concerning multitudes that thought themselves truly gracious and the friends of God and his children, that they are in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity. All the false colors and painting of hypocrites will then be taken off, and it shall appear what they be. Of many that have made a great show of religion and have been counted eminent saints, it shall appear that they never had one dram of grace in their hearts. There will be many dreadfully disappointed, when God comes to try them, that expected to be received and embraced in the arms of God’s eternal love; but God will say to them, “Depart from me, I know you not, you workers of iniquity” [Luke 13:27].  They thought they were friends, but they'll appear strangers and aliens, and it will signify nothing for 'em to plead that they have eaten and drunk in [his] presence, that he has taught in their hearts, that they have taught in his name, and in his name have done this or that.
Then the cloak of man’s own righteousness shall be taken off. It will appear then as filthy rags indeed and not sufficient to cover their nakedness. Rev. 16:15, “Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.”
And on the other hand, there will be many persons that have been hardly thought of, and censured as wicked men and called hypocrites, that then shall shine forth in the righteousness of Christ. God will commend them with a “well done, thou good and faithful servant [Matt. 25:21].” And many that have had many doubts concerning themselves and were afraid, and very like many that were afraid upon their deathbeds, when they come to be tried by the touchstone, shall be found true gold; and grace, which was small and almost invisible before, shall now be brought to perfection at that time. God, who searches the hearts and tries the reins, will examine concerning everyone, whether or no he ever with his whole [heart] received Jesus Christ, committed his soul unto him and with all his heart complied with the gospel; whether or no he chose Christ for his own sake and received [him], because of his own excellency and worthiness. God will try the state of every man by the same rules of his Word that he gives us, to try ourselves. Every one will be judged out of those things that are found written in the books. Thus, God will judge the secret state of the souls of men.
Second. Men’s thoughts and desires and counsels of their hearts must come into judgment before God. I Cor. 4:5, “When the Lord comes, he will bring to light the secret things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts.”
Men’s thoughts and the workings of their hearts are the most secret things that belong to men. ‘Tis one of the distinguishing attributes and prerogatives of God, to know men’s thoughts. Others may guess at them by men’s words and behavior, but God alone sees them. Rev. 2:23, “I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works.”
This province is quite out of the limits of all human judgments. Though men may sin exceedingly in their thoughts—they may do things only in their hearts, that are equal to many heinous sins in the outward behavior—yet such things are out of the reach of human view, and therefore out of the reach of human judgment.
Many men that have a fair outside and are orderly in their behavior that is seen of men, are yet licentious in their thoughts. There are many things that are restraints upon carnal men as to their outward carriage that may keep them tolerably orderly, such as fear of the punishment of human laws and fear of disgrace, being reputed as a vicious person. A respect to their own outward interest and common shame restrains, but these restraints take no hold of 'em, here. They may think what they please and indulge a sinful disposition in their thoughts as much as they please, and lose no credit or respect of men, nor be in any danger of it. They are quite secure in external acts of wickedness, let ‘em be never so secret, yet there is some danger of their being discovered. But here they are out of danger, except as sinful thoughts lead to sinful actions. And men are ready to think they may take a liberty in their thoughts, that they may indulge themselves there as long as they don’t proceed to the outward act.
But, however, all these secret hidden workings of heart must come into judgment; they must give an account of them. Though they can indulge their lusts in their thoughts as they go about the world and be secure from mortal eyes, yet their thoughts are written down in God’s book; they are not forgotten, but are written with a pen of iron and the point of a diamond. They must give an account of all their lewd, unclean thoughts, their vain thoughts, their covetous thoughts, their malicious and revengeful thoughts, and their thoughts about worldly and profane things upon the Sabbath.
There is abundance of sin in men’s thoughts. Many are continually working wickedness and contracting guilt by the inward meditations and desires of their hearts. They will find a dreadful account in God’s book another day, when the thoughts of their hearts shall be laid open, and they shall be recompensed according to these secret works of theirs.
The aims, designs and ends of men in all that they do must all come into judgment before God. The wickedness of actions arises very much from the wicked aims and designs that men have in them. Now other men can’t certainly determine this any otherwise than they infer it from the outward act; but God, by his own perfect knowledge, will determine with what aim and view every action was done, and precisely with how great a degree of wicked inclination and desire every action was performed, and so will proportion the punishment.
On the other hand, the gracious workings of the hearts of the godly must come into judgment. God will declare all their holy aspirations of soul after God and Jesus Christ, their gracious desires and longings of hearts, their secret acts of love, of holy delight, of submission and resignation; as also their charitable and benevolent thoughts towards their brethren, and all their good designs and views in what they did, and their good intentions and desires, where they han’t had opportunity to do according to their intentions. Those works that are done in secret, he that seeth in secret will openly reward [Matt. 6:4]. Much of the work of a Christian is heart work, consisting in the acting’s of the soul. But those works which none sees but God and the soul in which they are, shall be seen by heaven and earth in the day of judgment.
Third. God will judge men’s secret behavior. God’s eyes are everywhere, beholding the evil and the good; darkness is no covering to him. Roofs and walls that hide from the view of the world don’t hide from God; everything is transparent to his eyes, that are as a flame of fire. We know not how much sin there is committed in secret, but God knows, and will make known to all. “There is nothing hid that shall not be revealed, nor covered that shall not be known [Luke 12:2].”
Sin loves darkness. As it loves spiritual darkness, so it flies from the light of the sun. Therefore, wicked works in general are called “the works of darkness.” How much secret fraud and cheating is there in the world? How much lasciviousness and uncleanness, in the several degrees of it, are committed in secret? How much slander and evil-speaking and lying are men guilty of in secret? How many malicious and revengeful acts do men secretly perpetuate against their neighbors? See Job 24:13-17, “They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof. The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief. The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face. In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.”
Dreadful will be the account which we shall hear at the day of judgment of men’s secret sins and works of darkness. And dreadful will be the doom which shall be pronounced, and the punishment which shall be inflicted.
So the secret good works of the godly shall also be openly rewarded; their secret prayer, and praises, and humiliations, and their secret alms, and deeds of charity, Matt. 6:3[-4], “when thou dost alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret, himself shall reward thee openly.” All the secret piety, the secret diligence and watchfulness, and that holy commerce between God and him, though the world knows nothing of it, now shall be declared before men and angels, and God will honor them and glorify them in the sight of them all. Thus the secrets of men must be judged by God.  

APPLICATION.
I. Use of Reproof to those who take God’s work upon them in judging the secrets of men. There is a proneness in men, ever since the fall, to take God’s work upon them, to put themselves into God’s place, and to act the deity one towards another as far as they can. They will be each other lords and gods, and will take upon them to be the judges of others, and will not only judge those things that are apparent and open and liable to the cognizance of men, but they also assume to themselves to judge the secrets of men, those things that are invisible, and that it is God’s peculiar province to judge.
So they are forward to pass their judgment about the states of others’ souls, to determine that such and such visible Christians are hypocrites, that they have no true grace, but that they are wicked men. And they determine upon very slight grounds: as that they have done such and such things that ben’t right, and contrary to the rule, and so they at once conclude they are wicked men; or that they don’t tell of such particular experiences as some others do; they imagine they don’t talk like saints: and from many other things that ben’t sufficient grounds to judge a man a child of the devil.
There are many very forward to judge the hearts of others upon particular occasions and to censure ‘em, as if they could see their thoughts, intentions and designs. They are ready to put the hardest construction upon others’ actions, to judge severely of the motives and ends of such and such actions. They are especially ready to do it if they themselves have been displeased by ‘em, or if they have fallen into any sin, or have met with any great calamity. This is a very unchristian spirit, though it be a very common one; ‘tis exceeding contrary to the gospel rules. Rom. 14:4, “Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth”; as if he had said, “Who art thou[x] that you take upon you to act as lord and judge of your fellow creature and fellow servant?” So Jas. 4:[11-]12, “Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of his brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge. There is one lawgiver, that is able to save and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?”
When it is thus, it is a manifestation of a proud disposition, a disposition to exalt themselves above their fellow creatures and set themselves as their judges. It shows a very high opinion men have of themselves, and a great ignorance of their own failings and weakness, and a great deal of hypocrisy. Matt. 7:3-5, “why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.”
‘Tis a base spirit and hated by mankind, and even those persons that are most censorious will soonest be put into rage when others show the same spirit towards them.
Christ tells us that this is the way to be judged ourselves. If we are forward in judging and censuring others, we may not only expect to meet with the same from other men, but from God the great and rightful Judge. Matt. 7:1-2, “Judge not, that ye be not judged. For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.”
II. Use of Exhortation to sinners to reform their secret sins.
[First.] The sins that I speak of, are such, are hid from the eye of the world, either known only to you or known only to some that are concerned in the same sins. I fear there are many that now hear me whose hearts and consciences witness that they live in some secret, vicious practice. ‘Tis an encouragement to you to allow yourself in those ways of sin, that it is hidden from the world. But you must consider that that is not your advantage, but an advantage that Satan has to ruin and destroy you forever. When you can sin with the greatest security then Satan can work your ruin with the greatest ease. When you are secretly, indulging your sinful inclination, then Satan has the best opportunity to indulge his malice and inclination to destroy you. When he sees sinners bite securely at his bait, he then has the greatest hope of making a prey of ‘em, and has much the greatest advantage for it.
Consider what you have now heard: that all your secret sins that you from time to [time] commit are had in remembrance, everyone of them, and you must give an account to God about ‘em. They will all be brought to light, and will stand before you and stare you in the face, when you stand before God and before men and angels.
Consider also that, if you are got into a way of secretly gratifying any lust, your case is exceeding dangerous; there is great danger that you will so provoke God, and so harden your own heart, that you never will be effectually turned from sin to God. God often punishes men that live in ways of secret wickedness, especially under gospel light, by giving of them up forever to their own hearts’ lusts, Rom. 1:24-26. There is danger that you will provoke him, that he'll resolve never to give you conversion, if you han’t done it already. Doubtless there are a great many persons that seek to be converted that never obtain it in all their lives’ time, because they have so provoked God by allowed ways of secret wickedness, that he lets them alone and never will make a saving change in them. Is. 59:2, “your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.”
If you indulge yourself in sin, upon a presumption that God will show mercy to you hereafter, that is the way to have God resolve that he will not show you mercy, and that he will order matters for your ruin and destruction. The Apostle speaks of those that have abused the grace of God, and have taken encouragement from it to indulge themselves in lasciviousness, as you may see, Jude 4. And speaking of the great danger of their destruction, he compares, as you may see in the following verses, to those that were overthrown in the wilderness, that God swore should never enter into his rest, and to the fallen angels, and the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah [Jude 6-7].
O, therefore, beware! Go not on in that dismal road that you are in. Forsake those ways immediately, if you would not run yourself down so far towards eternal destruction, that you never shall be able to recover yourself.Second. Let all be exhorted to judge themselves, that they may not be judged of God hereafter. There are two parts of self-judging:
1. Considering our ways and condemning ourselves for our sins. We must thus judge our own secret sins. Judge therefore now, before that great Judge comes. Hearken to the judgment of conscience; be often in reflecting on your secret sins, and confess, and lament, and bewail them before God. Condemn your former sinful practices, not only in words but in heart, not only in saying that they are vile and odious but in hating and abhorring of them; and even that you deserve God’s wrath, that it would be just for God forever to deny you any mercy; and don’t only say so, but see and be deeply sensible of it.
2. Another part of self-judging is examining ourselves about our state, that we may judge what condition we are in, whether in a natural condition. This doctrine offers the strongest motive to us to do thus. We have heard that this is one of the secrets that is to be tried, and judged, and brought to light at the day of judgment, and according to which our state is to be determined forever. ‘Tis worth the while, therefore, to take the greatest care, and use the[xi] utmost diligence, that you may not be deceived and find yourself deluded when you come to be judged. Take heed you don’t flatter yourself that you are rich and increased with goods, while indeed you are wretched and miserable, and poor and blind and naked. Watch and keep your garments, lest you then walk naked and they see your shame. You can’t be too careful, too strict and exact in your inquiries about your own state and condition, because ‘tis a matter of great difficulty and of the greatest consequence. Never give over this work of trying and examining yourself, and using all possible proper means to find out the state of your own soul, till you have obtained full satisfaction. Never fix it down with yourself that your condition is good, so as to make it no more a question, till you are sure you can’t be deceived. The judgment that you are to be tried by hereafter will be most strict; let your trial of yourself be also very strict and severe.
[III. The] Last Use is to encourage godly men in their secret piety. For God, who sees in secret, will bring it into judgment and will reward it openly. ‘Tis the temper of sincere Christians; they don’t desire to publish abroad their good deeds and the acts of piety between God and their own souls. ‘Tis sufficient to them that God knows; it, they seek not so much the praise of men, as of God.
And God will honor them in the sight of the many millions that shall be present at the last day. You may take encouragement, therefore, from hence, to be more diligent and careful and fervent in spirit in your secret service of God, whatever reproaches and hard censures you may meet with from men. You may comfort yourself in this, that God is to be your judge, who is a righteous judge, and will reward you and everyone according to his works.
God don’t forget none of your prayers, nor none of your tears, none of your secret praises, none of your holy conversation that is in secret between God and you. He remembers every passage, and lays up a reward for you accordingly against you come into his presence.
What great encouragement is it to diligence, frequency and exactness, in walking with God in secret, that every gracious thought and every gracious act shall have an eternal reward; that your crown of glory, which shall be set upon your head at the day of judgment, will be proportionally bright and glistening to the exercises of that holy life that is hid with Christ in God.

Jonathan Edwards

rael of Old singled them Out from all the Nations that dwell upon the face of the Whole Earth Indeed the distinction is not so Great for they were the Only Visible Peo People that of God in the Cant such partition walls Whereby one single nation is separated from all the world. are broken down But Yet our nation has been in many Respects an Elect nation. that God has seemd to delight in peculiarly favouring.. both with Respect to Our their Religious and temporal Interests. and in the first Place La particular And If we Considerd how they have been favoured with Respect to their Religion and spiritual Concerns 1 They Are distinguished from the Greater part of mentioned that the world that have not the word of God Amongst them. I suppose There is more of the face of the Earth that is possessed and Inhabited by heathen than by those of all professions that own one only true and living God. some worship the sun moon & stars. and others Worship the devil that Comes and Appears in a bodily shape and others worship Images that themselves make others worship the Fire and others worship men. and others beasts.

___________________________________________

There are multitudes that besides offering multitude of beasts in sacrifice. they also offer up their Children. besides extraordinary Occasions they Yearly offer [^015-note1] up a Certain Number and in some Countreys Great multitudes Every Year.

________________________

in those Countreys Where satan Rules as God the service that he Requires is abundantly more Grievous than that which the true God agreable to the Cruel nature of the devil. very Generally in heathen Countreys some Great Pieces of Cruelty is a part of their Religion Part of the worship that is Required of them. Psal 74 20 The dark Places of the Earth Are full of the habitations of Cruelty.

__________________________

such Gross darkness in matters of Religion tends to make men ba and Generally does make them base barbarous and beastly in other things in the Com mon affairs of life. besides and so makes men miserable

____

of here besides the Eternal misery it brings w upon those Whole nations in another world. they are subject to satan while in this world as their God & they Are Given to him when they Go out of the world. they Are satans possession his vassals and slaves here and they Are the his Prey in Another world Life.

____________

How Great a mercy therefore is it to live free from such darkness and to have the knowledge of the true [-] true the living. the holy and mercifull God [^015-note2] the Case was the same once with Our nation. they were in heathenish darkness. And it was only because the sovereign Grace of God so Orderd that the Gospel Came to England. and did not Go to India and Tartary and Ethiop those Countreys bent so far distant from Judea from Whence the Gospel Came Resurrection as first f [^015-note3] as England is.

________________________________________________________

2 Our Nation Is distinguished from the far Greater Part of the world that dont Own Jesus X and that have not the light of the Gospel besides those Coun treys that Are darkened with Gross Idolatry. ther are Vast Tracks of the Earth that Are Overrun with Mohametanists that profess the Turkish Religion who tho they Own one only supream God Yet they deny Jesus X the mediatour and prefer Mohamet before him. And have the Alcoran Instead of the Bible. Judea is which once was the only Countrey favourd Satisfaction b with the true Religion is so. and so are all those Countreys that we Read on in the scripture. Par Babilon, & Persia and Egypt and Arabia and Syria, and Grecia. The Religion Established in all these Countreys is the Mohametan Religion. so it is in most of those Countreys where the Apostles Preachd the Gospel. Galatia and Corinth. & Ephesus [^015-note4] Philippis Philippi. and Colosse and Thessalonica and most of those Countreys they Apostles traveld in in that we read of in the Acts. the people the tho these Can Places were once famous for the Gospel yet the people that Now Possess them Are Mohometans. There Are Indeed a few Here and there that do yet Possess Xtianity tho tis mu much corrupted among them. and they miserably oppressed by [-] mahamatans. we Are distinguished from those that were for many Ag[e]s [^015-note5] Gods only People upon the face of the Whole Earth Who Are broken over from the fat olive of Which they B Are the natural branches an and we Are Grafted in . who have the Curse of God Upon them. for Above this seventeen hundred Years hardening of them. blinding their Eyes and keeping of them in an Obstinate Rejection of the Gospel.

_______________________________

3 God by his Goodness has distinguished Our Nation from Great Part of them that do Own Jesus X that Yet are under the Powers of Go strong delusions and Gross darkness. The Popishs Countreys tho they Call themselves Xtian yet are Countreys of Great darkness they wholly make the Gospel of Jesus X of none effect by their Errors and superstitions. that professedly depend upon their own Works their Religion is Great part of It It it Consists in Idolatry. and for the Greatest Part [^015-note6] in those things that God Never Commanded. and that are Contrary to the nature of Xtian worship.

___________________________________

The People Are Industriously kept in Great Ignorance for this End that they may the more patiently submit to all those Burthens Which their Priests Lay upon they them Which they themselves will not touch with one of their fingers for the Enriching and Advancing themselves. We Have free liberty of looking into the Word of God Which the People among them bent sufferd to see or have in their houses. we Have liberty of Joining in the Publick worship. but thei of God but their worship is in a Language the people dont Grace Justifiable Understan'd.

Our nation was once in the same Circumstances but God has deliverd us out of them has freed us from the popish Yoke. and deliverd us from Captivity to that spiritual Babilon. and from slavery to that spiritual Egypt. when many other nations are still Left in it that are Yet wandering after the Beast and Worshipping the Dragon.

4 Our Nation Is distinguished from Great Part of those that Profess the Protestant Religion. in b especially in these three things. 1. We have Liberty of the exercise of the true Religion without Persecution. and that many other Love to X Protestants have not in many other [^015-note7] Countreys they Are forced to meet togeth together in the wilderness to worship God together or hear his Word and have their T Enemies Carefully watching of them, bent sufferd to bring up their Children in their own Religion but have them violently taken away and Put to popish Instructors.

so it has been and Is still in many Parts of Germany and in Poland. While we in the mean time Enjoy liberty and may serve God without fear. we may weekly worship God according to our Consciences in Gods house and with his people and None makes us afraid. and not only so but 2

3 The Constitution of the nation is such that & Establishment of the Nation is such that none Are Capable of any the Civil Government but that are not of the Protestant Religion. so that our free exercise of Our Religion is secured to us by the Laws of the Realm. so that according to the ConSl stitution of the nation tis Impossible that a popish [^015-note10] King should Rule over us. or that Any of that Religion should be in any Post of Civil Government Whatsoever. And this Establishment has been C Preserved hitherto In spite of the est a a Great many Plots and devices to Overthrow it. in spite of all the Enemies of our nation it bo both in Our own nation and in other Nations. when they have been big with hopes and proud with Ex have triumphd in expectation of Accomplishing their design God has from time to time b disappointed them and sent them Away ashamed and has preserved the Religi Nation when its friends were so Gods people were full of fears and trembled in expectation of what was Coming.

Then the Waters had overwhelmed us Blessed be the Lord who has not Given us a prey to their teeth.

If it were so in our Nation and in this Land how Grievous ly should we take it and In this Countrey how Grievous ly should we take it.

we proceed in the Second Place to show how God in how two or three Particulars & how God has distinguished this Land

Luke 8 28 When he saw Jesus he Cried out

and fell down before him. and With a Loud voice

said Jesus thou son of God most high, I beseech

thee torment me not.

We have here An Account of a voiage that X took

across the sea of Galilee. otherwise Called the Lake of

Gennezareth. and of his Going over to the Countrey

of the Gaderenes . the Place that X Commonly Used

to Capernaum the Place that X Commonly Used to

Reside at was on one side of the Lake and Gadera

on the Place of the Gaderenes on the Other and When

he Came there he hi met him a man Possessed with

An Army of devils.

It was so ordered in providence that there should be a

Great many at that time Possessed with devils, that

X Jesus might have Occasion of manifesting his

messiahship. by and th by Casting of them out and

that he might Give a specimen of the work Which

he Came into the world for Which was to Cast out

Satan and deli out of mens hearts and out of the

World.

This seems to be X very design in taking this voyage

to Work this miracle in Casting out those devils

and thereby to show his Glory to the Gaderenes

and to the world. and when X Came ashore it was

so Order'd that the man met him he it seems [^027-note1]

he was not Possessed With One devil Only but

With a Great multitude and therefore When X

asks him What is his Name he Answers Legion.

Legion is a military term the Romans Used to divide

their Armies into Leg distingt Companies Which they

Called Legions i 600 horse or 6000 t foot were

a Legion. we we Are not and so the Armies of

hell are divided some Are busy in one place and

some in and some in Another. one these Legions

possessed this man. we Are not take it that there

Legion but a Certain is Put for An Uncertain and

the meaning is that there was a Great Company or

Army of devils.

The devils have a trembling Expectation of the

Compleating of their Punishment and of being dread-

fully destroyed some way or Other by Jesus X. as we

Read that the devils believe and tremble. James

2. 19. the devil Understood so much by the Prophi-

cies or Gods Parti either by Particular threatenings to

the devils as the Prophecies or both. that there

was a dreadfull destruction to Come Upon him by

to befall him. as Proud an and as scornfull as the de-

vil is he is not Above the fear of Gods wa wrath. he

has felt it he knows What it is and therefore he [^027-note2]

tuously Every day died and went to hell and

was there extremely miserable and tormented when

Common Opinion of their Extremi Greatness and

extremity as if People were needlessly frighted

About it some of them have Written to this pur-

pose . They Are Impatient of such a Restraint up

on their lusts. they devote themselves to their

P spoild by those fears & Checks of Conscience

they say they make the misery of hell to Consist prin-

cipally in the Punishment of Loss they shall be Cast

this world and the Pleasures of heaven .
